text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- National Council of Churches of Kenya re-ignites the reform debate in a major statement in which it describes the January 31 deadline for the issuing of new generation identity cards as unrealistic.
- Plans are at an advanced stage to establish family courts to handle matrimonial litigation.
- Kenyan police confirm that the suspect being sought in the case of the disappearance of 54 million shillings belonging to Citibank NA has left the country.
- An historic constitutional application seeking an order to compel Kenya's Chief Justice Abdul Majid Cockar to vacate office is instituted in the high court.
- Information Minister Johnstone Makau says a communication body will be established before the next general election to vet and regulate the licensing of radio and television stations.
- Central Bank of Kenya says strict rules will be applied this year to check government borrowing for the purposes of financing the 1997 general election.
- A senior criminal investigation department officer has gone underground following last Sunday's disappearance of 54 million shillings belonging to Citibank.
- FORD-Asili Chairman Kenneth Matiba renounces his political ties with Raila Odinga and says he is ready to meet President Daniel arap Moi with other opposition leaders.
